name: Will a pool removal affect drainage on the property?

mainEntity.name: Will removing an in-ground pool change drainage, runoff, or flooding risk on a Los Angeles property?
mainEntity.text: Will removing an in-ground pool change drainage, runoff, or flooding risk on a Los Angeles property?

acceptedAnswer.text: Pool removal often changes the site’s drainage pattern because a large recessed area is being replaced with compacted fill and a new grade. If the work is not planned carefully, water may run toward the house, pond in low spots, or erode the new soil after heavy rain. This is especially important in Los Angeles, where properties may have limited slope, hardscape, or hillside runoff issues. Homeowners should ask how the contractor will regrade the area, where water will flow after the pool is gone, and whether additional drains, swales, or surface adjustments are needed. Drainage should never be treated as an afterthought. A good removal project leaves the yard stable and dry, not just empty.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes. Pool removal can change how water moves across a yard, especially if the old pool acted like a low spot or if the backfill is not graded correctly. Poor drainage planning can cause pooling, erosion, or water toward the house. Final grading and drainage design should be part of the project.
